newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Tigers hand over body of dead N.Korean.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Tigers hand over body of dead N.Korean.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger separatists on Wednesday handed over to Red Cross officials the body of a dead North Korean crew member from a ship the rebels captured this week, International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) officials said.
"The dead body has been handed over to the ICRC and we are bringing it back to Colombo to be given to the shipping company," an ICRC spokesman told Reuters.
"The remaining crew will be handed over in the coming days. I cannot say when," the spokesman added.

Aid officials in the north said the body of Sin Jwang-ho, 54, the ship's fourth officer, had been brought to the hospital in government-held Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo. It was to be handed over to the shipping company on Thursday.

The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east, seized the North Korean ship Morang Bong late on Monday in the seas off Point Pedro on the former rebel stronghold of Jaffna.

The clandestine Voice of Tigers radio said on Tuesday that one of the ship's 38 crew was killed in a shoot-out when the crew tried to escape. The ship, chartered by private traders, had carried food and other essential supplies to the north.
Last week, LTTE rebels attacked and torched a refugee ship and took away its nine crew, including two Indonesians who were later released.
Sri Lankan troops killed more than 40 Tiger guerrillas in separate attacks near Nedunkerni in the heart of the guerrillas' northern Wanni stronghold, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.

Three soldiers were also killed and 18 were wounded when the Tigers attacked troops several times in places near Nedunkerni, 260 km (160 miles) northeast of Colombo, late on Tuesday, a ministry statement said.
"Ground troops confirm altogether more than 40 terrorists were definitely killed on this day and many wounded," it said.
Government forces last month captured Nedunkerni after a major offensive launched to open a supply route through the mostly shrub-covered Wanni.
Two deadly rebel attacks have since slowed the offensive.
In another incident, troops in an ambush killed two rebels at Pesalai in Mannar district, 240 km (150 miles) north of the capital, the statement said.
Two soldiers were also killed when the rebels retaliated, it added.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 13-year-old war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
